title: Compatible coefficient encodings and sheaf-level origin
statement: Use the module sites and exchange maps of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Let B be a finite discrete commutative ring killed by the prime ell, k a field of positive prime characteristic different from ell, and sq any commutative square of separated finite-type k-schemes. Given a family of monoidal identifications of its pulled-back condensed coefficient rings with the sheafified constant rings on all schemes and the constant-ring internal-module encoding hypothesis, there exist abelian coefficient equivalences E0 on X and E1 on Y-prime such that every constructible internal sheaf on X has etale sheaf origin under comparison inverse image followed by E0. Their concretely derived realization functors identify the four vertices and each of the three unit-square-counit arrows of exchange, on every bounded constructible realized complex. These are sheaf-origin and stepwise coherence assertions; no arbitrary bounded-complex origin or assembled arrow comparison is assumed.

proof.text: Use the supplied ring isomorphisms and the constant-ring internal module encoding. Construct one sectionwise encoding on all schemes and normalize against the canonical coefficient ring family; unrelated scalar-twisted choices must not be treated as coherent. The application supplies the canonical family constructed by inverse image from the point.

Transport finite local presentations on the finite constructible stratification to ordinary finite-coefficient module sheaves. Each presentation map is a finite matrix of locally constant B-valued sections. After one common refinement all entries are constant, so its cokernel is the constant sheaf of the corresponding finitely presented B-module, which is finite. Thus the original strata have locally constant finite restrictions. Apply finite-ring constructible sheaf origin (Tag 09AK).

Use the actual functorial comparison of inverse images and bounded-below qcqs direct images from the source library. The comparisons are adjunction mates: their unit, pullback-composition, and counit identities supply the three commuting squares. Every morphism here is qcqs. No exchange invertibility, properness, or Cartesian assumption is needed.
